# Agent environments

## What an environment is
State, observations, actions, dynamics. The reward is a separate claim about what matters.

## Partial observability (POMDP)
When the agent cannot see the full state it must maintain a belief and sometimes act to gather information. Measurement can be an action with a cost.

## Attention as a hidden variable
Learners do not read everything shown to them. Attention gates learning and drains with fatigue.

# Evaluating agents

## pass@k vs pass^k
pass@k: any of k runs succeeds. pass^k: all k succeed. Reliability is what deployment needs.

## Proxy vs direct measures
A quiz score is a proxy. Retention a week later is closer to the thing itself.

args.text:
Yes — use this in your writeup:

**pass^k** = the system succeeds on **all k runs**.

So if you test the same setup with 3 seeds, pass^3 is 1 only if **seed 1, seed 2, and seed 3 all succeed**; otherwise pass^3 = 0. It is stricter than **pass@k**, which counts success if **at least one** of the k runs succeeds.

A clean eval sentence you can paste:

“We evaluate reliability with **pass^k**, where a task counts as successful only if the agent succeeds on **all k seeded runs**. We report this over at least 3 seeds because pass^k measures consistency, whereas pass@k can hide unreliable behavior.”

args.text:
Yes — here’s the direct answer you can use:

**Why is this a POMDP?**
It is a POMDP because the assistant does **not** observe the full state of the environment. It can see only partial observations, like the current screen, messages, notes, or files it opens, while important variables such as the student’s **knowledge, attention, motivation, and whether they actually read something** are hidden. The assistant therefore has to infer that hidden state from observations and choose actions under uncertainty.

A short writeup version:

“This setting is a **POMDP** because the assistant has only partial observability of the true state. It can observe the screen and tool outputs, but hidden variables such as the student’s knowledge and attention are not directly visible. As a result, it must infer the student’s state from behavior and act under uncertainty.”

You already have a usable environment paragraph in your writeup now. Next, let’s make sure you can explain pass^k and POMDP out loud in 1 sentence each.
